items.original_context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: A category C consists of a collection of objects, morphisms assigned sources and targets, identity morphisms for every object, and associative composition of composable morphisms with those identities as two-sided units. The size and foundational status of each collection must be specified coherently; smallness and local smallness are additional conditions, not implicit parts of this generic formulation.

evidence.relevance: Explicit category axioms, but explicitly set-sized object set and Hom sets. Supports axioms, not unrestricted size.
Acknowledges proper-class object categories and carefully limits them to named examples. Does NOT generally certify every arbitrary class-sized category.

items.original_context: Category theory: ordinary functor between arbitrary categories C and D without assuming smallness; object/arrow assignments preserve identities and compositions.
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: For categories C and D in a shared foundational framework, a covariant functor F:C→D assigns each object x an object F(x), and each arrow f:x→y an arrow F(f):F(x)→F(y), preserving identities and every defined composition. No categorical smallness assumption is part of the abstract functor axioms, but functor assignment and category sizes must make sense in the chosen foundation.

evidence.relevance: Explicit object/arrow assignment and identity/composition preservation.
Shows that Stacks text principally assumes small categories, with selected big-category exceptions.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
items.definition_title: Quotient ring of a commutative unital ring
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: Let A be a commutative ring with identity, and I an ideal (not necessarily proper). The quotient ring A/I consists of cosets a+I and has operations (a+I)+(b+I)=(a+b)+I and (a+I)(b+I)=ab+I. Its unit is 1_A+I, and the canonical surjection A→A/I has kernel I.

evidence.relevance: Explicit coset quotient operations and zero-ring case A/A; source uses unital rings.
Commutative unital, zero ring admitted in algebraic-geometry convention.

items.original_context: Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: For an arbitrary function f:X→Y and B⊆Y, its inverse image f^{-1}[B] is the set {x∈X : f(x)∈B}. This is defined independently of whether f admits an inverse function.

evidence.relevance: Defines preimage for arbitrary maps and explicitly distinguishes from inverse functions.
Same set operation and explicit warning against assuming invertibility.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
items.definition_title: Polynomial ring in a set of commuting indeterminates
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: Given a commutative ring R with 1 and a set I, R[X_i:i∈I] is the R-algebra of formal finite sums ∑_α a_α X^α, where α:I→ℕ has finite support and only finitely many coefficients a_α are nonzero; addition is coefficientwise and multiplication is defined by distributive convolution. The variables commute and no variable evaluations are prescribed.

evidence.relevance: Explicit finite-variable polynomial ring and commuting-variable construction.

evidence.section: Ring of polynomials, indexed summary excerpt
evidence.relevance: Indexed reference describes arbitrarily many indeterminates with each polynomial involving finitely many variables. Direct source page temporarily inaccessible at lookup, so do not claim a full source review.

items.original_query: residue field of a local ring
items.original_context: Commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: residue field A/m of a commutative local ring (A,m), including the prime-localized κ(p)=R_p/pR_p and the scheme-point κ(s)=O_{S,s}/m_s.
items.definition_title: Residue field at a maximal or prime ideal
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: For a commutative local ring (A,m), its residue field is A/m. At a prime p of a commutative ring R, the residue field is κ(p)=R_p/pR_p, canonically the fraction field of R/p. For a scheme point x, the residue field is that of its local stalk.

evidence.relevance: Residue field of local ring, localized prime and field-of-fractions equivalence.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: associative commutative ring R with a specified multiplicative identity 1_R; the prime-ideal formulation does not assume the ring is an integral domain.
items.provisional_definition_paraphrase: A commutative unital ring is a set R with addition, multiplication and distinguished elements 0 and 1 such that (R,+,0) is an abelian group, multiplication is associative and commutative with multiplicative identity 1, and multiplication distributes over addition. Unless a nontriviality condition is explicitly imposed, the zero ring with 0=1 is included.

evidence.relevance: Ring axioms, commutativity and explicit inclusion of zero ring.
Confirms standard commutative-algebra ring convention, including zero ring in Stacks project.
